chapter: King Oliver, own trio and Kirby
title: How he came to join King Oliver through Dave Nelson
summary: Moore played the Nest Club with Dave Nelson, Oliver's nephew, who introduced him; Oliver ran a business-like band, 1929 to about 1937.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: So you made these recordings, and then you went off on the road with Joe Oliver. How long did you play with Joe Oliver?
From '29 on until he passed away. I think it was around '37, something like that...
So you were with him quite a little while. How was it that you started playing with him? Was it as with the musicians before, that he enjoyed your playing and asked you to play? Or what happened?
He was the trumpet player. And I was working with Dave Nelson about three or four nights at a place called the Nest.

The Nest Club. That was on 133rd Street. I started working there around five, I'd get out of there at eleven the next day. Play eight shows. People from downtown used to come up there. The place was packed every night. We'd come out of there with something... I was making forty dollars a week, and we'd come out of there with forty or fifty dollars in tips apiece. Dave Nelson liked how I played, so he introduced me to him. He was King Oliver's nephew, I mean... That was King Oliver's nephew, Dave Nelson was.
And he introduced me to King Oliver. He goes, "Yes, all right. Like your (?). I'm gonna start rehearsing next week. Bring 'em on down. Come and bring your drums on down."
And the (??) walk in there, brought my drums down... Because I'm always... For the rehearsal or the job, I'm always the first one there, so I can set up, you know. He introduced me to him.
King Oliver, though, he's got his own set way. He hardly ever smiled. This was a business to him. Make time and don't get drunk. Call the rehearsal when everybody's there.
